title: Measurement and Geometry - Lesson 7 Assessment: Pyramid Volume Exploration
description: Show understanding of pyramid volume by comparing matching prisms and pyramids and explaining the one-third factor.

questions.question: A pyramid and a prism have the same rectangular base and the same height. The prism volume is 96 cm^3. What is the pyramid volume?
questions.explanation: The matching pyramid has one-third of the prism volume, so 96 / 3 = 32 cm^3.

questions.question: A pyramid has base area 54 m^2 and height 5 m. What is its volume in m^3? Enter just the number.
A square pyramid has base side length 9 cm and height 8 cm. What is the first step to find its volume?
options: Find the base area by calculating 9 x 9.
Divide the height by 3 before finding the base area.
Find the perimeter by calculating 4 x 9.
questions.explanation: For a square base, first find B by squaring the side length: 9 x 9 = 81 cm^2.

questions.question: The height used in V = (1/3)Bh is the perpendicular distance from the base to the top point of the pyramid.
questions.explanation: Pyramid height is measured straight from the base to the top point, perpendicular to the base.

questions.question: A rectangular pyramid has base length 12 in, base width 5 in, and height 9 in. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: The base area is 12 x 5 = 60 in^2. Then V = (1/3)(60)(9) = 180 in^3.

questions.question: Three matching pyramids fill a prism with volume 420 cm^3. What is the volume of one pyramid in cm^3? Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: If three matching pyramids fill the prism, one pyramid has 420 / 3 = 140 cm^3.

questions.question: Which pair of solids can be compared directly using the one-third relationship?
options: A pyramid and a prism with the same base area and height
A prism and a cylinder with the same height only
Two pyramids with different bases and heights
questions.explanation: The one-third relationship works for a pyramid and a matching prism with the same base area and height.

questions.question: A rectangular pyramid has a base 7 cm by 6 cm and height 10 cm. What is its volume in cm^3? Enter just the number.
A student says a pyramid with base area 20 cm^2 and height 9 cm has volume 180 cm^3. Explain the mistake and give the correct volume.
questions.correctAnswer: The student found the matching prism volume by multiplying 20 x 9 but forgot to take one-third. The correct pyramid volume is (1/3)(20)(9) = 60 cm^3.
questions.explanation: For pyramids, Bh gives the matching prism volume. The pyramid volume is one-third of that amount.

questions.question: In your own words, explain why V = (1/3)Bh makes sense for a pyramid.
questions.correctAnswer: The formula makes sense because Bh is the volume of a prism with the same base area and height, and one pyramid takes up one-third of that matching prism. Three matching pyramids would fill the prism.
questions.explanation: A complete explanation should connect B and h to the matching prism and state that the pyramid is one-third of that prism.
